messages:
ana: heads-up: multiple customers complaining about increased tail latency on /v1/completions starting after the 2026-03-14 23:40 UTC deploy. p95 jumped from ~200ms to ~720ms, p99 to ~4.2s on rdx-13b-std. short repro below.

rob: saw it too in graphite. spike correlates with deploy tag runtime-199d. logs show kernel chooser selecting flash_attn_v3 by default for these models.

kevin: runtime-199d included nvcc flag change: added -DUSE_FAST_SMEM and updated kernel-tile heuristics. suspect memory-path change.

maria: can someone paste a runnable repro? i'll try to reproduce on a dev GPU.

ana: repro (batch=1, seq=1024, tokens=40):
```
ab -n 100 -c 5 -p payload.json -T application/json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
# payload.json: {"model":"rdx-13b-std","input":"hello" + "x"*1000,"max_tokens":40}
```
observed 99th percentile ~4s locally against canary. rdx-3b unaffected.

rob: runtime trace: kernel_selector: choosing flash_attn_v3 (est 1.1ms/token) fallback sdpa_opt. actual kernel timing shows a jump when seq > 600: kernel exec ~2.8ms/token and extra 500-800us memcpy on host.

kevin: digging into kernel logs - flash_attn_v3 introduced a staging buffer optimization that copies to pinned host memory for certain tile sizes. looks like our heuristic misfires for long contexts and larger batch interleavings.

maria: can we flip a runtime flag to prefer sdpa_opt for sequences >512? we have dynamic policy rules in model-kernel-config.

ops_oncall: temporary mitigation: add a runtime routing rule to prefer sdpa_opt for rdx-13b-std and rdx-7b-std, and enable extra headroom (more instances) to avoid latency amplification. I'll apply now.

build-bot: kernel-routing-update#456 deployed to canary set (3 hosts).

ops_oncall: canary metrics: p95 rdx-13b-std down from 720ms -> 240ms, p99 down from 4.2s -> 680ms. preparing prod roll in 10m if stable.

ana: thanks. we still need a root cause. kevin: can you run a bisect across runtime commits between 199a..199d and also compile variants to isolate nvcc flag impact?

kevin: starting bisect. early findings: the change that toggled USE_FAST_SMEM combined with a tile reflow change is the likely culprit. building variants: (A) with USE_FAST_SMEM off, (B) with original tiling, (C) both.

maria: i'll create an automated micro-benchmark that sweeps seq_len 128..2048, batch sizes 1..8 for flash_attn_v3 and sdpa_opt and uploads results to perfdb. add it to the CI matrix.

kevin: perf runs: variant A (disable fast smem) restores good behavior: p99 falls to ~650ms. variant B (original tiling) also helps but still has small memcpy. seems both changes together cause the pathological path.

rob: what's the long-term plan? upstream flash team might need a patch, but we should also harden our kernel-cost model.

maria: proposals: 1) revert nvcc flag (fast smem) in our builds until upstream fixes, 2) add sequence-length aware cost model so flash kernels are deprioritized for long contexts, 3) add unit tests that assert no p99 regressions for seq_len>=1024 on canary builds.

ops_oncall: immediate: rolling the kernel routing to prod now. medium: kevin to produce a debug runtime build with detailed kernel telemetry (KERNEL_PROFILE=1) and re-run perf on staging (ETA 3h). long: submit upstream issue + patch and update compile pipeline (ETA 1 week).

kevin: uploaded debug runtime to staging, running telemetry harness now. logs show flash_attn_v3 enters codepath `stage_to_pinned()` when tile_width >= 64, triggering a host<->device memcpy that wasn't amortized for single-request workloads.

maria: ok that explains the latency. let's also check if this causes OOMs or thrashing for 2k contexts. add long-context stress tests.

rob: I've notified affected customers with a short note: "We're aware of increased tail latency for some models after our recent deploy. We've applied a rollback-mitigation to prefer a stable kernel and are investigating the root cause. We'll follow up with timeline and permanent fix."

ops_oncall: incident ticket created INC-2026-129 with links to logs, perf graphs, and canary traces.

ana: action items recap:
- kevin: finish bisect and produce PR to revert USE_FAST_SMEM and tile reflow (ETA 4h)
- kevin: produce debug runtime build with KERNEL_PROFILE and full traces (ETA 3h)
- maria: add seq-length sweep perf test to CI and perfdb (ETA EOD)
- rob: monitor p95/p99 for next 48h, alert if p99 > 1s for any rdx-* model
- infra/ops: keep kernel-routing rule in place until we have a safe runtime build (ETA TBD)

kevin: bisect found the single offending commit that combined both changes. opening PR with revert and a safer opt-in flag for fast smem.

maria: once PR lands, we'll run end-to-end load tests before promoting. also adding a gating perf check.

ops_oncall: prod metrics stable after routing rule. closing initial escalation; will update thread when PR is merged and validated. :white_check_mark:
